title: Product overview + PRD: Redwood Optimize 1.3 & Roadmap, Pricing, Release Notes
author: Sofia Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This single-page product document summarizes the product overview for Redwood Optimize 1.3 (our cost/performance toolkit for inference), the PRD and requirements for the 1.3 release, high-level design specifications, roadmap and themes for the next three quarters, pricing and packaging guidance, and the initial release notes for v1.3. The audience is product, engineering, solutions, and go-to-market teams.

1) Product overview

h2. What is Redwood Optimize
Redwood Optimize is a suite of tools and recommendations that automatically identifies cost and latency optimizations for running inference on Redwood. Key capabilities include:
- Intelligent batching and caching configuration suggestions
- Model & quantization recommendations per workload
- Quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals
- Cost impact simulations and recommended rollout actions

h2. Target users and jobs-to-be-done
- ML Engineers: reduce per-token cost and maintain SLOs across model variants.
- Platform/Infra: apply standardized batching/caching policies across services.
- Product Managers: quantify unit economics changes and tradeoffs before rollouts.

h2. Success metrics (North Star for Optimize)
- % reduction in per-token cost for customers adopting recommendations (goal: 12% average across adopters within 90 days).
- Adoption rate: 30% of Dedicated customers enabling Optimize policies on at least one service within 6 months.
- False positive rate in quality regression alerts <= 5% (measured vs. manual eval).

2) PRD: Redwood Optimize v1.3 (summary)

h3. Objective
Deliver automated, actionable optimization recommendations for batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles, plus safe rollout controls (canary, A/B) that respect customers' latency SLOs.

h3. Key use-cases in scope for v1.3
- Per-route batching and dynamic batch-size suggestions based on measured latency distributions.
- KV cache recommendations (prefix vs. full request) with expected hit-rate and latency impact.
- Quantization profile suggestions: fp16, int8/4 candidates, with quality impact estimates tied to eval prompt-sets.
- Safe rollout: one-click canary with automatic rollback on user-defined quality or latency thresholds.

h3. Out of scope
- Model retraining or prompt rewriting suggestions (considered for later release).
- On-prem specific packaging changes (deferred to eng-private-deployments roadmap).

h3. Acceptance criteria (must be met before GA)
- Feature QA: Recommendations produced for 80% of sampled routes in internal benchmark traffic.
- Accuracy: Predicted latency/cost delta within +/- 15% of observed for recommended actions.
- Rollout safety: Canary framework can detect regressions within 15 minutes and auto-rollback.
- UX: Console exposes clear explanation for each recommendation and a one-click apply/canary flow.

h3. Ownership and stakeholders
- Product owner: Sofia Patel (product).
- Engineering lead: Ethan Li (eng-serving-runtime / optimize team).
- Research lead: Mariana Gomez (applied-ml-and-evals).
- GTM: Priya Shah (sales-enablement).

3) Requirements (functional and non-functional)

h4. Functional requirements
- FR-101: Generate batching suggestions per route including recommended min/max batch sizes, expected throughput increase, and expected 95th/99th latency change.
- FR-102: Provide cache configuration suggestions with predicted hit-rate and per-token cost reduction estimate.
- FR-103: Produce per-model quantization candidate list with per-prompt-set quality deltas and uncertainty estimate.
- FR-104: Expose canary/A-B rollout controls in Console with success criteria (latency and quality thresholds).
- FR-105: Export recommendations as JSON/CLI for infra automation.

h4. Non-functional requirements
- NFR-201: Recommendation generation job latency <= 300s for full route analysis on a 24-hour sample.
- NFR-202: System must store evaluation artifacts for at least 90 days (configurable).
- NFR-203: Predictions (cost/latency) must be explainable with provenance metadata (feature input list).
- NFR-204: Recommendation engine must respect data residency flags for private deployments.

h4. Data and privacy considerations
- Recommendation telemetry must be hashed and PII removed.
- Customer opt-in required for any sample traffic collection beyond metadata.
- For private deployments, recommendations must be computable offline without sending customer traces to Redwood cloud.

4) Design specifications (high-level)

h3. Architecture components
- Data Ingest: sampling agent (hosted or local) that aggregates per-route latency, token counts, and cache keys metadata.
- Analysis Engine: batch/ML models + heuristics that produce recommendations and uncertainty scores.
- Console UI & API: exposes recommendations, explanations, and rollout controls.
- Rollout Controller: implements canary rules, monitors SLOs, and triggers rollback or promote actions.

h3. API and config artifacts
- Recommendation JSON format (example):
  {
    "route": "string",
    "recommendations": ["batch_size": "int", "expected_cost_delta_pct": "float", "uncertainty": "float"]
  }
  (Note: payload above will be returned in actual API; internal format includes provenance strings.)

h3. Console UX notes
- Recommendations page shows: route, current config, recommended config, estimated cost delta, estimated latency delta, quality risk (low/medium/high), and confidence score.
- 'Preview canary' modal shows expected impact over the selected timespan and enables selecting traffic percentage and duration.

h3. Rollout & safety mechanisms
- Canary monitoring window: default 30 minutes, adjustable by user.
- Auto-rollback triggers: latency p95 increase > 15% OR quality-alerts > threshold (user-configured; default: any failed eval in canary).
- Manual override: operators can force promote after acknowledging risk.

5) Roadmap and themes (Q1 2026 – Q3 2026)

- Q1 2026 (current): GA for Optimize 1.3 (batching, caching, quantization recommendations + canary flows). Internal beta: Dec 2025; public beta: Jan 2026; GA: Feb 2026.
- Q2 2026: Integration with Dedicated autoscaling policies (predictive autoscale suggested configs), per-tenant cost reports, and expanded quantization profiles (int4 candidates).
- Q3 2026: Multi-model routing optimizer (cross-model batching and dynamic model selection), deeper private deployment support (air-gapped recommendation tooling), and advanced quality evaluation dashboard.

Cross-cutting themes
- Safety-first rollouts: every recommendation path must include guardrails and clear rollback.
- Explainability: provide simple, actionable explanations and proven delta estimates.
- Low-friction adoption: one-click canary and infrastructure-friendly JSON outputs.

6) Pricing & packaging notes

Positioning: Optimize is a paid add-on across Hosted and Dedicated. Pricing aims to capture value (cost savings and reduced operational effort) without blocking PLG adoption.

Proposed packaging (v1.3):
- Free tier: baseline recommendations and dashboards for small/test tenants (data-limited, no canary automation).
- Standard (add-on): $0.10 per 10k inference units analyzed per month + $500/month per account for advanced monitoring (example metric to be finalized by finance).
- Enterprise (bundle): custom pricing with Dedicated/Private deals; includes on-prem recommendation agent and 24/7 support.

Billing notes and signals
- Metering will be based on the number of routes and volume analyzed (inference units) and enabled rollouts.
- Offer a 90-day trial for standard tier to accelerate adoption.
- Discounting guidance: 10–20% discount for annual commitments or when purchased with Dedicated reserved capacity.

7) Release notes: Redwood Optimize v1.3 (GA 2026-02-15)

h3. Summary
GA release for Redwood Optimize v1.3: automated batching, cache, and quantization recommendations plus Console canary/A-B rollout controls. Primary aim: reduce per-token cost while preserving latency and quality SLOs.

h3. Notable changes
- New: Per-route batching recommendations with confidence scores.
- New: KV/prefix cache suggestions with hit-rate and cost delta estimates.
- New: Quantization candidate generation with per-prompt-set quality deltas and uncertainty estimation.
- New: Console canary UI and Rollout Controller automations.
- Improved: Recommendation API + JSON export for infra automation.

h3. Known issues & workarounds
- Known: Certain long-tail routes with extremely low QPS may produce noisy estimates. Workaround: increase sampling window to 7 days.
- Known: Private on-prem customers require manual installation of the sampling agent; automated packaging for air-gapped setups is scheduled for Q3.

h3. Rollout plan
1. Internal canary with three strategic customers (week 1 GA).
2. Open beta for self-serve customers with trial (week 2–4).
3. Full GA enablement for all account tiers (end of month), with account exec outreach for Dedicated customers.

8) Operational runbooks (summary pointers)

- Where to look: eng-platform/runbooks/recommendation-engine-runbook (pointer to deeper ops playbook).
- Escalation: on-call for Optimize: optimize-sre rotation (see eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets for SLO definitions).
- Key monitoring alerts: analysis job failures (>1% job failure rate in 24h), prediction drift (observed delta vs predicted > 25% for 3 routes), canary rollback triggers exceeded.

9) Next steps & open decisions
- Finalize per-10k inference unit price with finance (target: finalize by 2026-02-01).
- Validate default auto-rollback thresholds with reliability team and adjust for high-throughput customers.
- Plan for on-prem automated packaging and zero-data-leakage recommendation pipeline (Q3).
